messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: knitr notebook in action with rCharts
parts:
This would not have been possible without Yihui's incredible work in putting together an R Notebook as a Shiny app in knitr. For those of you who have not tried it yet, just type this.

app = system.file('shiny', package = 'knitr')
shiny::runApp(app)

and you will have a browser version of R Notebook.


Ramnath


On Thursday, May 2, 2013 11:08:27 PM UTC-4, Kenton Russell wrote:
I wanted to make sure everyone saw knitr notebook in action in this incredible work by Ramnath Vaidyanathan in this video http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MqMkCk-nc6k.  He live codes R in the browser using his rCharts to create d3/javascript charts.

I couldn't help myself and did another one http://youtu.be/BXn_GyldWPc.

Thanks Yihui for this!

Hi, Ramnath.  I'd been hearing about "shiny" for a while now, but hadn't had time to look into it.  When I saw your note, I thought this looks simple enough, so I gave it a try.  Unfortunately, I get an error:

    Error in replayPlot(x) : could not open file 'figure/graphics.png'

I gather that "system.file" must be trying to create the "figure" directory directly in the R-installation tree.  I COULD give myself permission to do that (on my own linux box), but I'm reluctant to do that.  Do you (or others) know of a way around this?  Or if I'm just missing the mark completely, please point me in the right direction. Thanks.

-- Mike

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: knitr notebook in action with rCharts
parts:
You can copy the 'shiny' directory to a place where you have the write
permission, e.g.

file.copy(system.file('shiny', package = 'knitr'), '~/tmp/', recursive = TRUE)
library(shiny)
runApp('~/tmp/shiny')

Regards,
Yihui
